metadata.sysdescription: Charon is a fortified USFP frontier outpost linking Norayne, Triton and Waypoint 46. Mining and industry support a growing naval presence, while asteroid fields, nebulae and scattered debris make patrols difficult and provide ample cover for hostile activity.

Charon Fwd Command.description: Charon Forward Command is the system’s main TSN military base, coordinating gate security, patrols and local defences. Its docking, refuelling, repair and ordnance facilities make it the operational centre of USFP activity on the Norayne frontier.

SY 101.description: SY 101 is a compact naval shipyard supporting Charon’s frontier fleet. It handles structural repairs, refits and maintenance for smaller combat vessels, reducing the need to send damaged ships deeper into USFP territory.

Corelia Mining.description: Corelia Mining is one of Charon’s largest mineral-processing operations, feeding raw materials into the system’s shipyards and factories. Though civilian, its output is closely tied to local military repair and construction.

RS 9992.description: RS 9992 is a classified USFP research station absent from normal civilian navigation records. It operates with restricted access and its own concealed defence platform; most personnel in Charon are officially expected not to ask what happens there.

Harrling Casinos.description: Harrling Casinos is Charon’s main civilian leisure station, providing gaming, food, accommodation and basic services to naval crews, miners and traders. Its glamour is modest, but on a hard frontier posting it rarely lacks customers.

Soulin Trading.description: Soulin Trading is Charon’s main commercial hub, offering docking, refuelling, repairs and a wide range of civilian and technical goods. It is a common stop for independent traders and off-duty crews.

1791638202475.name: Spot
1791638202475.description: Spot is a remote ringed planet beyond Charon’s main inhabited zone. Its broad rock-and-ice rings make it an unmistakable navigational landmark, while the surrounding debris and distance from regular traffic leave the area sparsely visited and poorly watched.
